candidates.rationale: Best fitness in the batch (10.336) with perfect stability, but IC fades every year, from 0.0250 in 2000 to 0.0010 in 2013. Both range bounds use the same 21-day window, so the ceiling reacts as fast as the floor. Highs are the more likely target of faster arbitrage as trading automated later in the sample, so lengthening only the high-side window to 42 slows the ceiling and tests whether that preserves signal later in the window.

Nearest archive neighbor sits at rho 0.780, just under the 0.80 cutoff, and shares the exact TS_MEAN($return, 10) momentum leg with this factor. That shared term likely drives the near-duplicate risk. Widening the momentum window to 21 days breaks the literal overlap while keeping the value-minus-momentum structure working memory flags as the strongest idea this round.

IC declines every year from 2010 to 2013 and turns negative in the final year (-0.0028), the only crack in an otherwise clean record. The 21-day dollar-volume denominator also drives a 0.729 correlation with an archived range/dollar-volume factor. A 63-day liquidity average is less noisy late in sample and reduces overlap with that neighbor, without touching the price-range numerator.

Working memory flags a prior reject that used plain RANK instead of CS_RANK on a roa expression, an operator slip rather than a real signal. This parent has the same issue: a bare $roa under plain RANK. Fixing the operator tests the fundamental's true cross-sectional standing and matches how every other factor in this batch ranks.

Nearest archive correlation is 0.779, just under the cutoff, against a plain 21-day dollar-volume factor, so this range-over-liquidity ratio is likely dominated by the same dollar-volume term. Working memory also flags this stochastic-range/dollar-volume lineage as saturated. Swapping the denominator to raw share volume removes the price-scaling overlap while keeping the range-per-unit-liquidity idea.

IC half-life is 3.0 days, far shorter than any other factor here, yet the window is 15 days, five times longer than the effect lasts. 2012 also shows a sharp break (-0.0149). Narrowing the window to 5 days matches the lookback to the real decay speed instead of averaging in stale price history, which should also help the elevated 0.273 turnover.

t-stat is the second-weakest in the batch (2.76), and IC turns negative in the calm 2003, 2005, 2007 stretch between two strong crisis periods. This factor also sits at rho 0.779 against a sibling range/dollar-volume factor, which is being decorrelated on its own side by a field change, so the more informative fix here is the weighting scheme. An exponential average reacts to real liquidity shifts faster than a flat 21-day mean.

IC is positive nearly every year through 2009, then negative in all four remaining years, 2010 through 2013, a clean structural break rather than noise. A 2-day reversal is the most crowded, fastest-arbitraged horizon in this signal family. Widening the delta window to 5 days moves the measurement to a less contested horizon and should also reduce the elevated 0.516 turnover.

Turnover is 0.598, the highest in the batch, against the weakest t-stat (2.08) and a half-life over 63 days, so the daily rank is churning on noise the signal does not carry. The denominator already smooths the range over 21 days but the numerator is a raw single-day range. Smoothing the numerator over 5 days should cut the churn while keeping the relative-range-expansion idea.

Stability is 0.57, the worst in the batch, with 6 of 14 years negative. The two deepest breaks, 2001 and 2009, land exactly on the two sharp market reversals in the window, the classic failure mode of long-horizon return-over-volatility momentum. Coverage is also the lowest here at 0.935. Shortening the window from 126 to 63 days reduces exposure to the crash-prone horizon and directly raises coverage.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

  1. 252-day windows on fundamentals (leverage delta, book_per_share/close, roa mean) caused all 3 coverage rejects this round (0.871-0.872 vs 0.90 needed). Keep fundamental-field windows at 126 days or less unless coverage is confirmed first.
  2. A rank-difference between a value signal (earnings yield) and short-term momentum (10-day mean return) scored far above everything else this round (fitness 7.07 vs next-best 0.82). This value-minus-momentum rank structure is worth extending with other value/momentum field pairs.
  3. Pure fundamental-ratio transforms with no market-based term (margin/turnover/roe-roa spread, asset_turnover delta, eps-delta over book_per_share) were the weakest cheap_screen rejects (|t| 0.31-0.70). Fundamentals alone are not clearing the screen this round.
  4. Pairing a fundamental with a return-based term did better but still missed once: roa times EMA(return,60) reached |t| 0.85, the closest cheap_screen miss. Refine the return-term side (different smoothing or window) rather than abandoning this pairing direction.
  5. Very short deltas (5-day) on slow-moving fundamentals (accrual_gap) scored among the weakest (|t| 0.55). Slow-moving fields need longer differencing windows to carry signal.
  6. Five of fifteen rejects duplicated 9 to 15 nodes of one already-archived stochastic-range / dollar-volume-range subtree. That lineage is saturated; branch into new structural forms instead of recombining it further.
  7. A bare field proposed next to its own rank transform ($roa vs RANK($roa)) is a near-guaranteed correlation reject (rho about 1.0). Changing only the wrapper around an already-archived field is not a new signal.
  8. One reject used plain RANK instead of CS_RANK on a 252-day roa mean. Verify cross-sectional operators are applied consistently so rejections reflect true signal quality, not an operator slip.
